questions.question: Define supply and state the law of supply with three reasons why it holds.
questions.expected_answer: Supply is the quantity of a good or service producers are willing and able to offer for sale at each possible price during a given period. Law of supply: other things remaining the same, as price rises quantity supplied rises, and as price falls quantity supplied falls (a direct relationship). Reasons: higher price means more profit per unit (profit motive); the cost of producing extra units rises, so more is produced only at higher prices; new producers enter and existing producers switch resources when the price rises.

questions.question: Using the schedule R4: 30, R8: 80, R12: 120, R16: 160, R20: 200 muffins per day, describe the supply curve and calculate producers' revenue if 120 are sold at R12.
questions.expected_answer: With price on the vertical axis and quantity supplied per day on the horizontal axis, the plotted points form a curve sloping upward from left to right, labelled S. Revenue = 12 × 120 = R1 440.

questions.question: State whether each causes a movement along or a shift of the supply curve, and the direction: (a) the price of muffins rises; (b) the price of flour rises; (c) bakers buy faster ovens; (d) a drought.
questions.expected_answer: (a) Movement up along the curve (increase in quantity supplied). (b) Shift to the left (decrease in supply, higher costs). (c) Shift to the right (increase in supply, better technology). (d) Shift to the left (decrease in supply, natural conditions).
